newsitem.title: POLAND: Lafarge buys Polish cement firm Wierzbica.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge buys Polish cement firm Wierzbica.

text.p: France's building material producer Lafarge has bought a 60-percent stake in Polish cement plant Wierzbica SA from National Investment Funds (NFIs), PAP news agency said on Monday.
PAP quoted spokesman of NFI 11 Maciej Tekielski as saying Lafarge bought a 33-percent stake in Wierzbica, central Poland, from NFI 11 and 27 percent from 14 other funds.

PAP said, according to unofficial calculations, Lafarge paid $18 million for the stake. It said Lafarge also offered to pay a total of $4.5 million for 15 percent of shares Wierzbica now held by its employees.
NFI officials were not immediately available for comment.
Lafarge signed the agreement to buy a 60-percent stake in Wierzbica in late July, but the transaction was concluded only last week.
PAP said Wierzbica had a net profit of 200,000 zlotys on 68.4-million-zloty-sales last year.
Following the transaction Lafarge holds 60 percent of Wierzbica, 25 percent is owned by the state treasury and 15 percent is controlled by employees.
Lafarge holds a majority stake in the Kujawy cement firm and holds 41 percent of Malogoszcz.
Kujawy, Malogoszcz and Wierzbica plants jointly have about a 22-percent domestic market share.
